ImageDescription.value:
Marble terminal bust of Homer

Roman copy after a lost Hellenistic original of the 2nd century BC From Baiae, in Italy Various portraits of the poet Homer are known, all of them created long after his death around 700 BC. The so-called Hellenistic blind-type is the most evocative of them all. The treatment of the hair and the facial features can be paralleled with the figures of the Great Altar at Pergamon, and the original of the type was perhaps created for the great library there.
